results.title: CSV vs JSON vs NDJSON — Which Format Should You Choose? | The Text Tool
results.content: # CSV vs JSON vs NDJSON — Which Format Should You Choose? CSV, JSON, and NDJSON all move data between systems, but they shine in different jobs. JSON is human-readable and perfect for nested shapes and APIs. NDJSON streams massive logs and events line-by-line without blowing memory. ## What exactly are CSV, JSON, and NDJSON? **NDJSON (Newline-Delimited JSON)** is a stream of JSON objects, one per line. **NDJSON**: + streams at scale, line-oriented tools (tail/grep) work, easy to append. − not a single JSON document, requires discipline for one-object-per-line and newline handling. NDJSON is similar to JSON in size yet excels in streaming; you can process gigabytes by piping line-by-line without ever loading it whole. * Flatten nested JSON before writing CSV; don’t cram arrays into cells without a plan. **1) Preflight cleanup.** Paste your data and run Zero-Width/Bidi Remover to strip invisible Unicode, then Normalize Newlines to unify line endings to LF. **2) Convert format.** For tabular → structured, convert CSV → JSON (array of objects) or CSV → NDJSON (one object per line). For structured → tabular, flatten JSON arrays/objects into columns before exporting CSV. 3. JSON array → CSV (flattened). Perfect for appending to log streams; each line is a JSON object. **Who consumes it?** Analysts love CSV; frontends and APIs love JSON; data engineering loves NDJSON. **Delimiter ambiguity:** If your CSV fields contain commas, quote them. In JSON/NDJSON, keep dates as ISO-8601 strings and validate on ingest. Keep a tiny fixture set that includes: a field with a comma, a quoted quote, a newline inside a cell, a nested JSON object, and a two-line NDJSON sample. Convert CSV → NDJSON and update downstream tools to consume one object per line. Migrating an API from NDJSON to JSON? * CSV: verify delimiter and quoting; test fields containing commas/newlines. * NDJSON: ensure exactly one JSON object per line; no blank lines. * When should I prefer CSV over JSON? * When is NDJSON better than JSON? Each line is a valid JSON object, but the whole file is not a single valid JSON array. Be explicit about CSV quoting and JSON escaping; validate samples before bulk jobs.
